subject: Temporary TTL variance & short-term restore window for HearthCare audit
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@hearthcare.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ben.todd@hearthcare.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary TTL variance + short restore window for upcoming audit

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick onboarding so far. We're consolidating our evidence packets for an external compliance review next week and need to confirm two related asks that affect HearthCare data in Redwood: 1) a temporary extension of log TTL from our standard 30 days to 90 days for the date range Apr 1 — May 31, 2026; and 2) a short-term restore window where Redwood would hold backups for an additional 14 days past the normal purge schedule so we can pull artifacts if requested by auditors.

We understand these are exceptions but given the timing of the audit and the audit firm's scope we need to lock this down by EOD Monday if possible. Attached is the auditor's request (hearthcare_audit_request_20260514.pdf) showing the exact artifacts they may request.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can apply a customer-level TTL variance for logs and backups?
- If so, what is the process (legal approval + ops implementation) and the expected lead time?
- Any limitations around subprocessor deletion schedules we should be aware of (subprocessors that handle backups/logs)?

Appreciate your help — small list of names included on cc.

Thanks,
Sara
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager
HearthCare Inc.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@hearthcare.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary TTL variance + short restore window for upcoming audit

Sara —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Short answer: we can usually support a scoped exception, but it requires a legal sign-off + ops coordination with the subprocessor retention windows. I'll loop in Karthik (serving/runtime ops) and Laura (legal) to outline the steps and timeline.

Prelim notes:
- TTL variance for logs: feasible at the customer level if limited to a defined date range; we’ll need to ensure any subprocessor that stores logs can honor the hold.
- Backup retention / short-term restore: we can stage a hold on future purge jobs for the affected snapshots for up to 14 days, but that also depends on the backup subprocessor’s purge cadence and whether the snapshot has already been offloaded.

Karthik — can you confirm which subprocessors would be in the loop for HearthCare (based on their tenancy) and whether we can implement a 90-day log hold retroactively for Apr 1–May 31? If there are any immutable snapshot constraints or escrow timing issues we should call them out.

Laura — from a contract perspective, what minimal language do we need signed to approve a short-term retention exception (we can use an exception template attached)? Ideally we’d capture this in a short addendum and a signed DocuSign envelope so ops can act.

I’ve attached the auditor request for context.

—Kimberly
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary TTL variance + short restore window for upcoming audit

Kimberly / team —

I pulled the tenancy map for HearthCare. Relevant subprocessors: S3-ArchiveCo (offsite snapshot store), LogRelay (centralized log aggregator), and VaultSync (key material sync for encrypted backups). I attached the current subprocessor-delete-schedule.csv exported from our ops inventory.

Technical constraints and proposed approach:
1) Retroactive log hold (Apr 1–May 31): LogRelay keeps raw ingestion for 30 days; we can request a one-off retention override for that range but it will be processed as a manual retention flag on the aggregated chunks. Lead time: 48–72 hours to confirm availability and to complete the retention flag, since it touches a subprocessor ticket.

2) Backup snapshot hold: Snapshots that have already been archived to S3-ArchiveCo may require a retrieval + staged hold. If a snapshot is still within the local 7–14 day staging window, we can flip a hold and prevent the purge. If it’s already offloaded, we need S3-ArchiveCo to apply an additional hold; their SLA for manual holds is 3 business days.

3) Delete choreography with subprocessors: We will create a subprocessor hold ticket (OPS-HOLD-XXXX) referencing HearthCare account id HC-4892. That ticket will include the date range and artifact list and will attach a copy of the signed exception.

Operational impact: modest — expected small storage bump for the month. No code changes. We should scope the exception narrowly (only the artifacts on the auditor request) to limit exposure.

Attachments: subprocessor-delete-schedule.csv

I can start the ticket as soon as legal confirms the approval format.

—Karthik
Senior Platform Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@hearthcare.com>, Ben Todd <ben.todd@hearthcare.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary TTL variance + short restore window for upcoming audit

Thanks for the details. From a legal/compliance side: we can approve a narrow, timeboxed exception with these guardrails:

- Scope: explicit list of artifacts (snapshots, audit logs) and date range Apr 1–May 31, 2026. No general hold on all logs.
- Duration: up to 14-day extended hold for targeted snapshots; a 90-day log retention only for the specified date range.
- Approvals: HearthCare must sign the attached "retention-exception-template.docx" addendum and the Redwood DocuSign envelope. Addendum must include a statement that HearthCare acknowledges the temporary retention is for compliance review only and will expire automatically on the date specified.
- Subprocessor acknowledgment: ops will create OPS-HOLD-XXXX and attach this signed addendum; subprocessor SLAs documented in subprocessor-delete-schedule.csv will apply to any manual steps.

If you want, I can author the addendum and start a DocuSign envelope today. Please confirm whether HearthCare will sign electronically (DocuSign) and whether Ben/Tenant legal will countersign.

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Todd <ben.todd@hearthcare.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary TTL variance + short restore window for upcoming audit

Laura / Kimberly / Karthik —

Thanks — HearthCare confirms we will sign the addendum and countersign via DocuSign. Ben (legal) will complete the signature by Monday morning. We appreciate the narrow scope and the OPS-HOLD workflow. Once you open OPS-HOLD-XXXX, please tag me so I can provide the auditor artifact IDs if the ticket needs them.

Two small clarifications: 1) can the log hold be applied at a per-service namespace rather than account-wide? That helps us avoid retaining unrelated diagnostics; 2) will Redwood surface an estimated incremental storage cost for the hold so we can budget approval internally?

We will sign the DocuSign envelope.

—Ben Todd
Legal Ops Lead
HearthCare Inc.
